title: FSR: Independent Hardware Voltage Monitor

standards_mappings.rationale: Functional safety requirement from safety goal

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Synthetic FSR for independent HW monitor (addresses FTTI violation)

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Separated this functional safety requirement (ISO 26262 Part 4) from FB2-HW-TSR-000004 (Part 5), which carried identical statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria, and made the shared 'All cells (or representative subset >= 50%)' coverage criterion measurable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000027. This record now states the safety intent and only acceptance criteria that a test can decide from the item's observable behaviour: that the reaction is retained while the main microcontroller is held in reset (100 percent of overvoltage test points), the independent detection latency of 50 ms, and the 50 mV threshold accuracy. The structural properties - which rails, references, driver stages and comparators are shared with the main chain, and how many cells the independent chain covers - are hardware design properties and now live only in FB2-HW-TSR-000004, which states the hardware obligation with its own hardware acceptance criteria. The coverage criterion is resolved to 100 percent of the cells the main measurement chain monitors: the 'representative subset >= 50%' branch was rejected because 'representative subset' is undefined, no selection method is recorded anywhere in the corpus, and a subset would leave cells with no barrier against a main-path failure, which is the barrier's purpose. The 100 percent figure follows the precedent already used by FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 ('All cell voltages acquired / Cell count match / 100 / %'). The feasibility of a full independent divider network is NOT asserted: FB2-ASM-008 already records it as 'Requires PCB space, separate power domain, additional BOM cost. Feasibility to be confirmed', and that assumption is unchanged by this revision. The ASIL (ASIL_B), the safety_goal_ref, the statement's 50 ms and the verification approach are unchanged. The 115 ms figure in the rationale was removed in the same revision under finding FB2-REV-FND-000026. Removed the 115 ms figure from the rationale and replaced it with arithmetic derived from the corpus's own parameter registry. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000026 reported 115 ms as appearing in no record; that part of its evidence is corrected here. The figure is real but stale: it is the sum of a superseded allocation recorded in FB2-REV-000001 (as_is vertical-slice review, embedded finding FB2-FND-000001) as 'FSR-001 specifies 10 Hz (100 ms); FSR-002 specifies 10 ms check; FSR-003 specifies 5 ms contactor; sum = 115 ms'. 100 + 10 + 5 = 115. The allocation has since changed - FB2-PRM-000003 now gives afe_acquisition_period_ms = 50 and FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 allocates 25 ms for acquisition - so the figure no longer describes anything in this corpus. The justification is now stated on figures that still hold: the main path is 85 ms of the 100 ms interval; at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the contactor chain is 5 + 40 + 5 = 50 ms and the main path is 95 ms; and if detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 (50 ms) rather than the 25 ms allocated, the main path is 85 - 25 + 50 = 110 ms and overruns the interval. A main-path-only reaction therefore has no tolerance for a degraded contactor or for one acquisition period, which is the substantive argument for a second barrier and does not need the 115 ms. FB2-ASM-008's rationale carried the same stale figure and was corrected in the same pass.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the fault_reaction this requirement was missing. AR-005 is one of the four elements the FSC allocates a reaction to, and the reaction is the second barrier itself: open the contactors from the independent path, without waiting for the main microcontroller, at 50 ms, which is FB2-PRM-000007. The field records that this budget is an ALTERNATIVE to the main path's and not an addition to it - the two sum to 135 ms against a 100 ms interval, which is why the FSC and TSC both justify the barrier as a sensitivity on the main path (85 ms nominal, 95 ms at the FB2-PRM-000005 upper tolerance, 110 ms if detection waits a full acquisition period) rather than as a sum. mode_dependence states the property the concepts both insist on: there is no mode arbitration in this path, so in MOD-004 a hardware false positive disconnects a moving vehicle with no software able to intervene, and that is why the 50 mV threshold accuracy is a safety requirement in its own right. open_limits states the limit that dominates this record: the independence the reaction depends on is FB2-ASM-008, an assumption, is not demonstrated anywhere in this corpus, and the TSC names the absence of that demonstration as the largest open assumption of the ASIL D allocation. Revision 2 -> 3. Statement, rationale, all three acceptance criteria, safety_allocation including the ASIL_B allocation, feasibility_dependencies and the safety goal reference are unchanged and no threshold was relaxed. Human approval remains pending, production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false.

statement: The item shall maintain, as a second barrier to the ASIL D cell-voltage safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, a cell-overvoltage detection and HV-contactor-opening capability that is independent of the main measurement, decision and command path, so that a failure confined to the main path does not remove the overvoltage reaction; the capability shall be allocated ASIL B and shall produce its contactor-open request within 50 ms of the overvoltage it detects.
rationale: Provides freedom from interference for the ASIL D safety goal: a main-path-only reaction leaves no tolerance in the 100 ms interval. As allocated in FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 the main path is 85 ms (25 acquisition + 5 SPI + 2 PEC + 3 publish + 5 SOA check + 2 classification + 3 state transition + 5 coil command + 30 mechanical + 5 feedback), which leaves 15 ms. At the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the contactor chain is 5 + 40 + 5 = 50 ms and the main path is 95 ms, leaving 5 ms. If detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 (50 ms) instead of the 25 ms allocated, the main path is 85 - 25 + 50 = 110 ms and overruns the interval. A parallel ASIL B path with its own 50 ms budget (FB2-PRM-000007) is therefore the second barrier, not an optimisation. This functional requirement states the safety intent and the behaviour that decides it; the hardware obligation and the structural independence properties are specified by FB2-HW-TSR-000004, and the system-level separation is specified by FB2-SYS-SYR-000005.

acceptance_criteria.measure: Overvoltage test points at which the contactor-open request is still produced while the main microcontroller is held in reset, with no processing resource, no supply rail and no communication path of the main microcontroller available to the reaction
Time from the overvoltage being detected by the independent capability to its contactor-open request
Difference between the overvoltage threshold the independent capability realises and the configured cell shutdown threshold

fault_reaction.reaction: Open the HV contactors directly from the independent path, without passing through the main microcontroller and without waiting for the main path's decision. This is the reaction FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 allocates to AR-005 at 50 ms, and it is the reason AR-005 exists: if the main path AR-001 to AR-004 fails, this is the only reaction left that still opens the contactors. Its 50 ms budget is FB2-PRM-000007 (independent_monitor_latency_ms = 50, tolerance 40..60) and it is an ALTERNATIVE to the main path's budget, not an addition to it - FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.ftti_and_timing_budget.arithmetic_check says so in words: the two budgets are alternatives, not a sum. Adding them would give 135 ms against a 100 ms interval, which is why the arithmetic that justifies the barrier is stated as a sensitivity on the main path rather than as a sum of the two.
fault_reaction.triggered_by: The independent monitor's own hardware threshold being exceeded, measured through its own dividers and compared by its own comparator. It is not triggered by the main path's classification and it does not wait for one.
fault_reaction.mode_dependence: No mode arbitration exists in this path, and both concepts record that as a property to be stated rather than assumed. It acts whenever its own threshold is exceeded. In MOD-004 that means a hardware false positive disconnects a moving vehicle with no arbitration, no confirmation step and no way for software to intervene, which is why the 50 mV threshold accuracy acceptance criterion of this requirement is a safety requirement in its own right and not only a specification detail. It is also why the allowance is a deliberate margin: FB2-PRM-000001 carries a 1 mV absolute tolerance on cell_voltage_max, so the two independent thresholds cannot be expected to agree more closely than the components' own tolerances, and a monitor that triggered on a cell the main path considers acceptable would be a false reaction that disconnects a vehicle rather than a conservative one.
fault_reaction.allocation_basis: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.fault_reaction entry 2 ('Open the contactors through the independent path, without waiting for the main MCU', element_id AR-005, reaction_time_budget_ms 50). The same element and budget appear in FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.fault_reaction, which adds that the actuation output is separate from the main chain. The 50 ms is FB2-PRM-000007 and is the budget FB2-HW-TSR-000004 carries. The argument for the barrier is the arithmetic in this record's rationale: the main path is 85 ms of the 100 ms interval, 95 ms at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005, and 110 ms if detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 (50 ms) instead of the 25 ms allocated. A main-path-only reaction therefore has no tolerance for a degraded contactor or for one acquisition period.
fault_reaction.open_limits: The independence this reaction depends on is an assumption and is not demonstrated anywhere in this corpus. FB2-ASM-008 records that separate dividers, a separate power domain and separate actuation are required and that feasibility is to be confirmed. FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions states the consequence if it is unmet - the independent monitor becomes a second channel with the same failure modes as the first, two agreeing channels would be read as corroboration when they are one channel twice, and the safety goal would have no surviving barrier - and states in the same entry that the absence of a demonstration is the largest open assumption of the ASIL D allocation. FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.diagnostic_coverage_assumptions gives this mechanism a justification_basis of synthetic_assumption with an empty verification_record_refs list. FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 is the dependent-failure analysis that records the residual common-cause exposure without quantifying it. The 50 ms is an allocated budget: no schematic, no BOM, no analysis and no measurement of the independent chain exists.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Independent power, sensing, and actuation path
